title: Mods
summary: JayV has a mod system, like games do: every mod is a package with a version and an author that adds to the app through its extension points. Today they are LLM engines (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Kilo Code, OpenRouter, LiteLLM), agents (like Ollama and LM Studio) and optional features: statistics, gatehouse board, live files, chat search, project notes, second opinion, plan before building, parallel agents, earlier answers, lean code, symbol index, MCP, skills, skills.sh and find in conversation. A mod can also bring skills that Jev picks by the request, like REA for reverse engineering. One mod can bring several of them and need other mods. Every mod lives in the public repository jayv-coder-mods and reaches the app and the site as a catalog; when you sign in, only the essential mods install themselves, turned on; the LLM engines, the agents and the skills wait in the catalog on the site for whoever wants them. Each mod has its own page on the site, with what it does, how to install it and how to use it.
usage: Open Settings › Mods. Each mod shows its icon. The installed mods are in two tabs, each with its count: in Installed, with the mods you chose, turn each one on or off, open its settings or uninstall it; Essentials has the mods JayV keeps installed and on. To install a mod, open its page on the site, signed in, choose the environment and click Install in JayV: the site saves it in your account and asks the app to sync right away, and the mod shows up in Installed, turned on, with the mods it needs. An uninstall waits in the list, with Undo, until you save. Search filters both tabs by name, description or author. The essential mods — the features of the app — always stay installed and on, without a switch or Uninstall; the LLM engines, the agents (like Ollama and LM Studio) and the skills (like REA) can be turned off and uninstalled. The changes apply when you save, in this environment and on your other computers; the site (Dashboard › Mods) shows and changes the same mods. A mod that came installed does not come back on its own after you uninstall it. A mod that needs a newer JayV waits for the update. Your plan still decides: what it doesn't include stays off, and what it locks stays on. The book button of each mod opens its page on the site. Also in the command palette (Ctrl+K): Settings › Mods › Installed, Settings › Mods › Essentials, Turn on mod, Turn off mod, Uninstall mod and Mod page on the site. If another computer or the site changes the mods while you have unsaved changes here, saving applies only what you changed in the tab.
